notes: The EIA August 2026 pipeline projects workbook, Natural Gas Pipeline Projects sheet, Excel row 126, says Transco Power Express is aimed at Northern Virginia data center markets. No single campus is named. TC Energy's chief executive said, as reported by DatacenterDynamics in May 2025, that the Northwoods project is designed to serve power generation demand in the Midwest, including data centers. No specific data center campus or shipper is named, so this is medium confidence. A DatacenterDynamics article from May 2025 quotes TC Energy's chief executive saying the Northwoods project on the ANR system is designed to serve electric generation demand in the US Midwest, including data centers. It names no single campus.

No existing row matches. The Rover Pipeline rows are the connecting line, not this lateral. A July 2026 Bowling Green Independent Media report says Williams is installing the Apollo South Pipeline, a 20-inch high-pressure gas line from the Rover Pipeline in southern Wood County, Ohio to the power plant on Mercer Road in Middleton Township. The plant's only power customer is Meta, which ties the line to its data center. Construction was planned to start in September 2026. The Williams project page for the Apollo project lists an Apollo South Pipeline and an Apollo North Pipeline as separate filings, which supports the name and the sponsor. Williams filed the Ohio Power Siting Board notice under case 26-0624-GA-BLN, according to the earlier candidate notes; that case number was not confirmed on the pages read. Length was not found in any source read. The Ohio case record was not reachable, so length is left blank, not guessed. Status is proposed because no source read confirms that construction has begun. The Apollo North Pipeline (case 26-0275-GA-BLN) is a separate line and was not researched here. Owner is the Williams subsidiary named in the filing, written in the ownership team's style. Route not researched; no route is available.

This is a new pipeline with no row in the database. The Energy Cooperative of Newark, Ohio, a member-owned gas utility, is proposing a 24-mile, 24-inch steel line in Licking County. The utility's own project page says it would serve a behind-the-meter power plant for an off-grid data center and lists Ohio Power Siting Board case 26-769-GA-BLN. A local news report from late July 2026 says EdgeConneX's PowerConneX is paying for the roughly 160 million dollar line and names the New Albany data center. An earlier March 2026 report gave 150 million dollars. I used the later figure. Phase 1 runs from near Granville to the plant in New Albany and is scheduled for completion in September 2027. Phase 2 runs from Granville to near Hebron to reach a large transmission pipeline and is scheduled for 2028. Most Phase 1 easements are secured. A June 2026 Farm and Dairy report says the proposed 430 MW PowerConneX III plant would need a new 24-mile, 24-inch pipeline, which matches this line. The July report ties the line to the 216 MW PowerConneX II plant, so the plant it serves is not fully settled. The alias PowerConneX III gas supply pipeline comes only from the Farm and Dairy page, which describes the line but does not use that exact name. It may be a different pipeline, so treat the alias as tentative. Capacity was not found. Start and end points are approximate. No downloadable route was found. The owner spelling was not matched to the ownership team gazetteer, so the name is kept as the sources state it. Confidence is high for existence, sponsor, length, diameter and data center tie, and medium for cost and dates. The OPSB docket page was not read.

pipeline: Vector Gas Pipeline / Vector 2028 Westbound Expansion
notes: Enbridge and DT Midstream sanctioned an added 400 million cubic feet per day of westbound capacity on Vector, with service in 2028 (Enbridge story, May 2026). The EIA August 2026 workbook, sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Excel row 131, lists the project as Vector Pipeline Expansion, status Applied, 400 MMcf/d, 2028. It is not an existing row. The parent Vector Gas Pipeline (P0277) is operating, and the Blue Water rows (P2505, P3202) are older, separate projects. Guardian (P8171) is a different pipeline. Length is not stated anywhere found. EIA leaves it blank and the scope is likely compression plus loops, so length and diameter are left blank until a filing gives them. No FERC filing for the Vector expansion was located. Status is proposed because it is not yet built. DataCenter is yes from the EIA August 2026 workbook (Natural Gas Pipeline Projects sheet, Excel row 131). Its Demand Served column for this project says "Power / data centers (Chicago market)", and its notes say the expansion is driven by coal plant retirements plus data center load. That is a statement about this project, the same basis used for the Crossroads expansion. No data center campus or shipper is named, so the tag is medium confidence. Enbridge says the capacity serves utility demand. The 2028 year is the target in-service year, so it goes in StartYear1, not ProposalYear. The Natural Gas Intelligence article could not be read for the data center claim. Owner is the Vector Pipeline partnership, 60 percent Enbridge and 40 percent DT Midstream per Enbridge. The legal form LP is from the sponsor name in the queue and was not checked in a registry. Medium confidence: two sources agree on size and timing, none gives route or length.

Joule Capital Partners applied to Millard County, Utah, for a development agreement to build a 24-inch natural gas transmission pipeline from the Holden area to the McCornick area. The county planning commission notice is for a hearing on May 7, 2026. The notice does not name the data center or Kern River. Holden is where Kern River's mainline runs near the Delta Lateral tap. A Cleanview profile of the Joule data center campus from January 2026 says the campus will connect to the Kern River mainline through redundant 36-inch interconnections, so the tie to the campus comes from that profile and the applicant being the campus developer. The county notice says 24-inch and the profile says 36-inch, so it is not certain these are the same line. Length was not found and no route was found. Status is proposed because no approval or construction was found. Operator not found. Owner name not in the owner list. Separate from the Kern River Delta Lateral (P3856).
